messages:
Alex: Quick check — after the RFC merge we should follow up on region penalty decay. Current runtime holds a flat +10s latency penalty for 10m and ops is seeing long-tail failovers. Thoughts?
Maria: Yep, saw that in the dashboard this morning. Suggest: separate penalty magnitude from TTL and make decay exponential with a floor so short spikes don't linger.
Sanjay: Agree on separation. Also want tenant_priority to be able to opt out of cost-based penalties for enterprise SKUs.
Linda: We need to avoid per-request policy-eval spikes. Can we compute the heavy stuff at admission and cache a lightweight decision for the router?
Alex: Cache is fine but invalidation gets tricky. Prefer versioned cache keys + policy generation id.
Maria: Draft policy sketch:
```yaml
penalties:
  latency_ms: 10000
  decay: exp
  half_life_secs: 120
  minimum_ms: 200
  ttl_secs: 600
overrides:
  enterprise:
    cost_penalty: 0.0
    priority_boost: 0.8
```
Sanjay: Questions: 1) how do we ship this to runtime (sidecar vs inproc)? 2) how do we handle mixed-version clients during rollout?
Linda: Implementation notes: ship as small protobuf deltas. Sidecar subscribes to delta stream; inproc loads a snapshot from local store with a small watcher. For mixed-version clients, runtime falls back to compatibility shim that maps older fields.
Alex: Proposed migration plan: (a) policy serializer + versioning (b) runtime reader API + compatibility layer (c) cache key versioning + eviction strategy (d) canary on dev region + perf test.
Maria: Timeline estimate: serializer 2w, runtime reader + shim 1w, canary + evaluation 1w. I'll own the eval harness.
Alex: @ops-bot can we schedule a synthetic spike perf-run in dev-region to validate decay/ttl interplay?
ops-bot: Scheduled perf-run: dev-region load-test on 2026-04-02T09:00Z. Test config: 10k qps, 5% error-injection, 30m run. :white_check_mark:
Sanjay: Eval checklist: backfill 7 days of traffic with synthetic latency spikes, measure SLO regression <1%, check tail latency P99/P999, ensure no cost regression >3%.
Maria: I'll add the harness cases and share the runbook in the doc. Also will add a quick simulator to tweak half_life and ttl before rollout.
Linda: One more: we should add a telemetry flag so we can count how often enterprise override is used — helps with future pricing conversations.
Alex: Good call. We'll add metric: routing.policy.override.enterprise.count and routing.policy.cache.hit_rate.
Maria: I'll aim to post the initial eval results in this thread when available.
Alex: Thanks all. Sync tomorrow 11:00 to lock API surface and cut the first serializer CL. :thumbsup:
